arxiv-1711-04194.title: Full-Body Locomotion Reconstruction of Virtual Characters Using a Single IMU Journal: Sensors
arxiv-1711-04194.creator: Christos Mousas
arxiv-1711-04194.description: Abstract This paper presents a method of reconstructing full-body locomotion sequences for virtual characters in real-time, using data from a single inertial measurement unit (IMU). This process can be characterized by its difficulty because of the need to reconstruct a high number of degrees of freedom (DOFs) from a very low number of DOFs.

arxiv-2109-07829.title: Embeddings of anisotropic Besov spaces into Sobolev spaces
arxiv-2109-07829.creator: David Bartusel, Hartmut Führ
arxiv-2109-07829.description: Abstract . We study the embeddings of (homogeneous and inhomogeneous) anisotropic Besov spaces associated to an expansive matrix A A into Sobolev spaces, with focus on the influence of A A on the embedding behaviour. For a large range of parameters, we derive sharp characterizations of embeddings. Keywords: anisotropic Besov spaces; decomposition spaces; quasi-norms; coarse equivalence.

arxiv-2111-04342.title: Electroweak phase transition and gravitational waves in a two-component dark matter model
arxiv-2111-04342.creator: Ahmad Mohamadnejad
arxiv-2111-04342.description: Abstract We investigate an extension of the Standard Model (SM) with two candidates for dark matter (DM). One of them is a real scalar field and the other is an Abelian gauge field. Except for these two, there is another beyond SM field which has unit charge under a dark U D ​ ( 1 ) U_{D}(1) gauge symmetry.

arxiv-2201-12028.title: Multiple DP-coloring of planar graphs without 3-cycles and normally adjacent 4-cycles
arxiv-2201-12028.creator: Huan Zhou, Xuding Zhu
arxiv-2201-12028.description: Abstract The concept of DP-coloring of a graph is a generalization of list coloring introduced by Dvořák and Postle in 2015. Multiple DP-coloring of graphs, as a generalization of multiple list coloring, was first studied by Bernshteyn, Kostochka and Zhu in 2019.

arxiv-2202-10003.title: Sender-controlled measurement-device-independent multiparty quantum communication
arxiv-2202-10003.creator: Yuyan Wei 1 , Siying Wang 1 , Yajing Zhu 1 , and Tao Li 1,2
arxiv-2202-10003.description: Abstract Multiparty quantum communication is an important branch of quantum networks. It enables private information transmission with information-theoretic security among legitimate parties. We propose a sender-controlled measurement-device-independent multiparty quantum communication protocol. The sender Alice divides a private message into several parts and delivers them to different receivers for secret sharing with imperfect measurement devices and untrusted ancillary nodes.

arxiv-2203-04591.title: Yield-stress transition in suspensions of deformable droplets
arxiv-2203-04591.creator: Giuseppe Negro 1 , Livio Nicola Carenza 2 , Giuseppe Gonnella 1 , Fraser Mackay 3 , Alexander Morozov 3 , Davide Marenduzzo 3
arxiv-2203-04591.description: Abstract Yield-stress materials, which require a sufficiently large forcing to flow, are currently ill-understood theoretically. To gain insight into their yielding transition, here we study numerically the rheology of a suspension of deformable droplets under pressure-driven flow. We show that the suspension displays yield-stress behaviour, with the droplets remaining motionless when the applied body-force is below a critical value.

arxiv-2210-13991.title: A new class of exactly-solvable potentials by means of the hypergeometric equation
arxiv-2210-13991.creator: Wei Yang
arxiv-2210-13991.description: Abstract We obtained a new class of exactly-solvable potentials by means of the hypergeometric equation for Schrödinger equation, which different from the exactly-solvable potentials introduced by Bose and Natanzon. Using the new class of solvable potentials, we can obtain the corresponding complex PT-invariant potentials. This method can also apply to the other Fuchs equations. Emails: weiyang@glut.edu.

arxiv-2305-10395.title: Motion Planning (In)feasibility Detection using a Prior Roadmap via Path and Cut Search
arxiv-2305-10395.creator: Yoonchang Sung 1 and Peter Stone 1,2
arxiv-2305-10395.description: Abstract Motion planning seeks a collision-free path in a configuration space (C-space), representing all possible robot configurations in the environment. As it is challenging to construct a C-space explicitly for a high-dimensional robot, we generally build a graph structure called a roadmap , a discrete approximation of a complex continuous C-space, to reason about connectivity.

arxiv-2401-09505.title: Polarity switch of PMMA powder transported through a PMMA duct
arxiv-2401-09505.creator: Wenchao Xu 1, Holger Grosshans 1,2
arxiv-2401-09505.description: Abstract During pneumatic conveying, powder electrifies rapidly due to the high flow velocities. In our experiments, the particles even charge if the conveying duct is made of the same material, which might be caused by triboelectrification between two asymmetric contact surfaces. Surprisingly, we found the airflow rate to determine the polarity of the overall powder charge.

arxiv-2503-07526.title: DL _ \_ POLY 5: Calculation of system properties on the fly for very large systems via massive parallelism Journal: Computer Physics Communications
arxiv-2503-07526.creator: H. L. Devereux 1 , C. Cockrell 1,2 , A. M. Elena 3 , Ian Bush 4,6 , Aidan B. G. Chalk 5 , Jim Madge 3,7 , Ivan Scivetti 3 , J. S. Wilkins 4,6 , I. T. Todorov 1,3 , W. Smith 3 , K. Trachenko 1
arxiv-2503-07526.description: Abstract Modelling has become a third distinct line of scientific enquiry, alongside experiments and theory. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations serve to interpret, predict and guide experiments and to test and develop theories. A major limiting factor of MD simulations is system size and in particular the difficulty in handling, storing and processing trajectories of very large systems.

arxiv-2505-12049.title: Beyond Scalar Rewards: An Axiomatic Framework for Lexicographic MDPs
arxiv-2505-12049.creator: Mehran Shakerinava *, Siamak Ravanbakhsh, Adam Oberman
arxiv-2505-12049.description: Abstract Recent work has formalized the reward hypothesis through the lens of expected utility theory, by interpreting reward as utility. Hausner’s foundational work showed that dropping the continuity axiom leads to a generalization of expected utility theory where utilities are lexicographically ordered vectors of arbitrary dimension.

arxiv-2508-10877.title: The Dark Energy Bedrock All-Sky Supernova Program: Cross Calibration, Simulations, and Cosmology Forecasts
arxiv-2508-10877.creator: Maria Acevedo, Nora F. Sherman, Dillon Brout, Bastien Carreres, Daniel Scolnic, Brodie Popovic, Patrick Armstrong, Dingyuan Cao, Rebecca C. Chen, Alex Drlica-Wagner, Peter S. Ferguson, Christopher Lidman, Bailey Martin, Erik R. Peterson, Adam G. Riess
arxiv-2508-10877.description: Abstract Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) have been essential for probing the nature of dark energy; however, most SN analyses rely on the same low-redshift sample, which may lead to shared systematics. In a companion paper ( Sherman et al.

arxiv-2509-22428.title: Privacy Mechanism Design based on Empirical Distributions This work was supported by the Swedish Research Council (VR) under grants 2023-04787 and 2024-06615.
arxiv-2509-22428.creator: Leonhard Grosse 1 , Sara Saeidian 1 2 , Tobias J. Oechtering 1 , and Mikael Skoglund 1
arxiv-2509-22428.description: Abstract Pointwise maximal leakage (PML) is a per-outcome privacy measure based on threat models from quantitative information flow. Privacy guarantees with PML rely on knowledge about the distribution that generated the private data. In this work, we propose a framework for PML privacy assessment and mechanism design with empirical estimates of this data-generating distribution.

arxiv-2509-25054.title: Signaling in the Age of AI: Evidence from Cover Letters We are grateful to Elliot Ash for suggesting the research question and Freelancer.com for providing the data. We build on Galdin and Silbert 2024 who first measured similarity between cover letters and job posts on Freelancer.com, interpreted i
arxiv-2509-25054.creator: Jingyi Cui, Gabriel Dias, Justin Ye
arxiv-2509-25054.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jingyi Cui, Gabriel Dias, Justin Ye. We study how generative AI affects labor market signaling using the introduction of an AI-powered cover letter writing tool on Freelancer.com. Our data track both access to the tool and usage at the application level. Difference-in-differences estimates show that access to the AI tool increased textual alignment between cover letters and job posts—which we refer to as cover letter tailoring—and raised callback likelihoods.

arxiv-2602-09760.title: Improving Interpretability of Lexical Semantic Change with Neurobiological Features
arxiv-2602-09760.creator: Kohei Oda Hiroya Takamura Kiyoaki Shirai Natthawut Kertkeidkachorn
arxiv-2602-09760.description: Abstract Lexical Semantic Change (LSC) is the phenomenon in which the meaning of a word change over time. Most studies on LSC focus on improving the performance of estimating the degree of LSC, however, it is often difficult to interpret how the meaning of a word change.

britannica-1911-remainder-reversion.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-remainder-reversion.description: Article 'Remainder, Reversion' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 23), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. law a remainder or reversion is classed either as an incorporeal hereditament or, with greater correctness, as an estate in expectancy. That is to say, it is a present interest subject to an existing estate in possession called the particular estate, which must determine before the estate in expectancy can become an estate in possession.

pmc-10517702.title: Engineered Polymeric Nanovector for Intracellular Peptide Delivery in Antitumor Therapy
pmc-10517702.creator: Xi Zhang, Mingming Zhang, Sijun Huang, Kiyoshi Ohtani, Li Xu, Yi Guo
pmc-10517702.description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to deliver a polypeptide from the Bax-BH3 domain (BHP) through the synthesis of self-assembled amphiphile nanovectors (NVs) and to assess their potential for cancer therapeutic applications and biological safety in vitro and in vivo. These findings provide valuable options for cancer intervention and a novel approach for the rational design of therapeutics.

pmc-10575364.title: PhysioKit: An Open-Source, Low-Cost Physiological Computing Toolkit for Single- and Multi-User Studies
pmc-10575364.creator: Jitesh Joshi, Katherine Wang, Youngjun Cho, Massimo Mischi
pmc-10575364.description: The proliferation of physiological sensors opens new opportunities to explore interactions, conduct experiments and evaluate the user experience with continuous monitoring of bodily functions. Commercial devices, however, can be costly or limit access to raw waveform data, while low-cost sensors are efforts-intensive to setup. To address these challenges, we introduce PhysioKit, an open-source, low-cost physiological computing toolkit.

pmc-10705839.title: Cutaneous Mucormycosis in a Young Immunocompetent Trauma Patient: A Case Report
pmc-10705839.creator: André Silva, Christine Paiva, João Pedro Baptista, Rui Almeida, Rita Alves
pmc-10705839.description: IntroductionMucormycosis, a rare and life-threatening infection, is caused by microorganisms of the Mucorales order. It affects almost exclusively immunocompromised and diabetic patients, requiring extensive surgical debridement and prolonged antifungal therapy.Discussion/ResultsWe report the case of a 26-year-old immunocompetent woman, presenting with cutaneous mucormycosis after suffering blunt force trauma.

pmc-10738462.title: CONSIDERING HOSPITAL CLOSURES IN ALABAMA: NATIONAL POLICY IMPLICATIONS
pmc-10738462.creator: Avani Shah, Joseph Swain, Hailey Lewy
pmc-10738462.description: Hospital closures have increased over the past 10 years nationally, particularly in rural areas and states that did not receive Medicaid expansion funds (American Hospital Association). These closures can impact older adults health care, employment opportunities, and mortality rates. Recently, the Alabama Hospital Association reported that 12 hospitals are at risk of closing.

pmc-11692987.title: DEVELOPING A TAILORED STRAIN INDEX FOR LONG-DISTANCE FAMILY CAREGIVERS OF PERSONS WITH DEMENTIA
pmc-11692987.creator: Francesca Falzarano, Verena Cimarolli, Kathrin Boerner, Richard Chunga
pmc-11692987.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Most research has examined the experiences and consequences of dementia family caregiving among proximate caregivers, while the unique needs of the growing number of long-distance caregivers (LDCs) remain understudied. Since the vast majority of research and evidence-based intervention efforts have specifically focused on caregivers who reside in close proximity to their care-recipients, existing measures of caregiver strain do not adequately capture the unique distance-related challenges experienced by LDCs.

pmc-12428491.title: New Insights in Assessing AKI 3 Risk Factors and Predictors Associated with On-Pump Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement
pmc-12428491.creator: Anca Drăgan, Adrian Ştefan Drăgan
pmc-12428491.description: Background: Acute kidney injury (AKI) following cardiac surgery can lead to chronic kidney disease, increased hospitalization costs, and higher mortality risk. Our retrospective study identified risk factors of severe AKI (AKI 3) in patients undergoing on-pump surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR). Additionally, we analyzed the significance of inflammatory indexes and risk scores in predicting AKI 3, focusing on sex differences.

pmc-12448123.title: A noncanonical role of glycolytic metabolites controlling the timing of mouse embryo segmentation
pmc-12448123.creator: Hidenobu Miyazawa, Jona Rada, Nicole Prior, Paul Gerald Layague Sanchez, Emilia Esposito, Daria Bunina, Charles Girardot, Judith Zaugg, Alexander Aulehla
pmc-12448123.description: Studies on the impact of metabolism on cell fate decisions are seeing a renaissance. However, a key challenge remains to distinguish signaling functions of metabolism from its canonical bioenergetic and biosynthetic roles, which underlie cellular homeostasis. Here, we tackled this challenge using mouse embryonic axis segmentation as an experimental model.

The answers were processed by statistical analysis.Results221 of 314 respondents (70.

pmc-12706036.title: Triaxial test investigation of the reinforcement effect of Acacia dealbata roots on mountain red soil
pmc-12706036.creator: Xirui Dai, Zongheng xu, Hongchen Ye, Yun Zeng
pmc-12706036.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Vegetation roots play a pivotal role in enhancing the shear resistance and stability of degraded mountain red soils, yet the quantitative effects of root density and orientation remain poorly constrained. In this study, unconsolidated undrained triaxial tests were conducted on red soil reinforced with Acacia dealbata roots to examine the influence of root area ratio (RAR), spatial arrangement, and confining pressure on stress–strain behaviour and shear strength.
